(The Show)

Clue

A dinner party. A storm. A body. And everyone is lying.

Clue, live on stage, close enough to see who flinches.

The cult-classic murder mystery leaps from screen to stage in the basement of one of Soho’s best-kept secrets. Six strangers, one mansion and a night that gets worse by the minute. It’s fast, funny and gloriously silly, and you’ll spend the whole evening trying to work out who did it.

Based on the Paramount Pictures film and the Hasbro board game CLUE.

(04) Our story

“Before I knew what a spotlight, a microphone, or a theatre was there were two people who made me fall in love with the simple act of storytelling.”

Henry Calvert, founder

I grew up in rural North Yorkshire, not exactly a bustling hub for theatre in the UK, so like many, my first introduction to musical theatre was through classic movie musicals. Every weekend I’d gather in front of the TV in my grandparents’ living room and get lost in The Band Wagon, Funny Face, Seven Brides for Seven Brothers and of course Singin’ in the Rain. Seeing people have so much fun, singing and dancing, whilst bringing so much joy to my grandparents, made me realise that all I wanted to do for the rest of my life was dance like Fred Astaire, sing like Howard Keel and make ’em laugh like Donald O’Connor.

It was my grandparents that nurtured that dream. Whether it be through debating the lore of Dune with my Grandad, or my Grandma’s insistence on still calling me Billy Elliot, I am always reminded of the power of stories to bring us together, to dream, and to tell our own stories.

My grandparents encouraged me to no end, to tell my story and support others to tell theirs. At VTW we believe a great story can come from anywhere and everyone should have the chance to tell that story. It is with this ethos that we carry into all of our work. A focus on uplifting new and exciting talent in the realms of performance and writing through our live shows, and a real effort to bring younger people into the world of theatre through our education branch.

If you’re a creative, a writer, an actor, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.

We are always looking for new and exciting talent to work with and stories to tell. I can’t wait to see what we create together next.

(The founder)

Henry
Calvert

HeadshotComing soon

Henry is a content creator, presenter, journalist and performer from North Yorkshire, known for his northern charm and passion for all things pop culture.

Henry has garnered over half a million followers across his social platforms, through his viral skits and interviews with Hollywood A-listers like Jeff Goldblum, Jonathan Bailey and Jason Momoa. His authenticity and natural enthusiasm has led him to being trusted by and working with leading brands like Disney, Universal, and LEGO.

With a background in theatre, Henry’s transition from digital personality to presenter came naturally. He currently hosts Sky’s social series Gold Statue Energy, as well as hosting stages at conventions for both Disney and eBay. His love of theatre led him to develop his own live shows, and after a number of sold-out solo stand-up / cabaret style events, he made his West End debut hosting The Phoenix Theatre’s Gala Fundraiser.

Alongside his social media work and live shows, Henry is also a writer for SFX magazine, completing articles covering everything from set visits, musicals and interviews with leading cast and creatives, which has only served to solidify Henry as one of the most well-trusted voices within the pop culture space.

“TikTok’s favourite Geek”

About VTW

VTW Productions, short for Valerie & Tom Webster Productions, is a new London theatre company founded by Henry Calvert. Its first production is a stage version of the cult murder-mystery Clue at the Phoenix Artist Club in Soho, 5–20 March 2027.

(Production) A Northern Concert

Notes from
a Bottle

The best of northern talent, in the spirit of a classic northern pub.

When8, 15 & 27 Oct 2027
WhereYork Theatre Royal, Old Paint Shop
Seats75
Tickets£15
(The concept)

Northern
talent

Musicians, performers and musical theatre writers from the north, in one evening.

The concert highlights the breadth of talent coming out of the north of England. It grew from a showcase of Joel Priest’s new musical, Pint Painted Pictures, whose cast of mainly northern professional performers are also developing work of their own.

Pints is set in Sheffield and follows four seemingly stereotypical northern boys heading to London to watch their team win the play-off final. It dissects those stereotypes and relationships, with themes including drug use, sexuality and, of course, drinking.

(The evening)

The
format

Expect the atmosphere of a classic northern pub: old friends telling nostalgic stories and singing songs that feel like going out in Sheffield, Manchester or Leeds for the first time.

The night is hosted by presenter and content creator Henry Calvert, who also plays Dan in Pints. With around 20 minutes of the musical to showcase, from fully staged group numbers to intimate solos, each song in character leads into a moment for that performer’s own music.

You will leave with a real feel for what Pints, and the north, is all about: community, friendship and good music.

(In rehearsal)

Rehearsals for the Pint Painted Pictures scratch night, Sheffield Theatre’s Open Works Festival.

(The performers)
Writer, Performer

Joel Priest

After a sold-out concert production of his first musical, Between the Sheets (Crazy Coqs), Joel is back with Pint Painted Pictures, which drew overwhelmingly positive feedback at Sheffield Theatre’s Open Works Festival.

Host, Performer

Henry Calvert

Returns to the stage after his sold-out solo show at Crazy Coqs, as host and as Dan in Pints. For five years one of the most trusted creators in pop culture, with 500K+ followers, and a presenter for outlets including Sky and the BBC.

Performer, Musician

Will Callan

Stage credits include Marius in Les Misérables (Sondheim Theatre) and Sebastian in Cruel Intentions (UK Tour). Plays Jake in Pints and makes pop, soul and R&B music as CALLAN.

Performer

Luke Ray

Fresh out of GSA, with theatre and short film credits. Brings real grounding to the character of Lewis in Pints.

Performer, Musician

Eve Maidwell

Trained at Trinity Laban. Performed in Connections the Musical (The Other Palace) and choreographed A Christmas Carol (Erasmus Theatre). A singer-songwriter with an EP on the way.

(05) Education

Education

Lighting the creative fire in the next generation.

(Why it matters)

The
spark

For young people, experiencing theatre for the first time is simply the spark that lights the creative fire.

At VTW we believe that making a conscious, in-person effort to encourage and nurture this fire is the most important thing. Unfortunately, careers in the arts can often feel unattainable for young people, whether through geographical or financial barriers. Training is consistently expensive and more often than not is only readily available in big cities.

So at VTW we are proud to bring our expertise to schools and universities across the country. Whether it is singing lessons with young boys who’ve never seen another bloke sing musical theatre before, or workshops on developing a personal brand with sixth formers, regardless of age or educational level, we offer insights into a plethora of career options within the performing arts.
